title: Representational Geometry of Harmful vs. Benign Dual-Use Knowledge

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong: if intent-sensitive representations exist internally, monitoring can go beyond keyword matching. If no such signal exists, refusal is purely behavioral and brittle. Either finding has significant safety implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: constructing paired educational/adversarial prompts and extracting SAE features is feasible with SAELens. Clustering analysis and probe training follow standard workflows. Dataset construction requires care but not advanced skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple dual-use topic areas each requiring paired prompt construction, plus clustering and probing analysis across areas creates sustained effort. Could narrow to 1-2 topics for 30 hours but the proposal spans several.

novelty.reasoning: The representational separation between safe and unsafe prompts has been established by multiple papers (single refusal direction, concept cones, fine-tuning collapse studies). However, the specific focus on dual-use knowledge — where the factual content is identical but intent differs — and whether SAE features can distinguish educational from adversarial framing of the same information is a more targeted question that has not been fully addressed.

evidence.source: The Geometry of Refusal in LLMs: Concept Cones and Representational Independence (2025)
evidence.finding: Analyzes representational geometry of refusal, proposing concept cones as a framework for understanding how harmful vs. benign content is separated in activation space.

evidence.source: Why LLM Safety Guardrails Collapse After Fine-tuning (2025)
evidence.finding: Shows that representation similarity between alignment data and fine-tuning data predicts safety guardrail collapse, establishing that safe/unsafe content has measurably different representational geometry.

evidence.source: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction (NeurIPS 2024)
evidence.finding: Identifies a single direction mediating refusal that implicitly separates harmful from benign requests in activation space.
